# Convert Video to HEVC (H.265)

- Route: `/tools/convert-video-to-hevc`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `video`
- Slug: `convert-video-to-hevc`

## Summary

Re-encode any video as H.265 for roughly half the file size of H.264 at the same quality, for storage, 4K and modern devices. (Video tools)

## Details

HEVC, also called H.265, is the successor to H.264. At the same visual quality it needs around 40 to 50 percent fewer bits, which is why phones record 4K in it and why it is the format of choice for archiving footage. Media Manipulator re-encodes any video to HEVC on our servers with FFmpeg's x265 encoder at the quality level you pick, in an MP4 container that iPhones, Macs, Windows 10+, Android and modern TVs all play.
### What it does
- Re-encodes any input video as H.265 in an MP4 container.
- Three quality presets mapped to CRF values; file size roughly halves versus H.264.
- Keeps resolution and frame rate; optionally downsizes 4K to 1080p for a far smaller file.
- Audio is re-encoded as AAC.
### How to use it
1. Upload a video: Any common format, including H.264 MP4.
2. Pick a quality: Smallest, balanced or high quality.
3. Convert: x265 encodes on our servers; slower than H.264.
4. Download: Save the .mp4 with HEVC inside.
### Supported formats
- Input: mp4, mov, mkv, webm, avi, m4v, flv, wmv
- Output: mp4
- HEVC encoding is CPU-heavy; expect several minutes for long or 4K sources.
### Technical details
- Encoded with libx265 at CRF 28 (balanced), 32 (smallest) or 24 (high quality), medium preset, hvc1 tag for Apple compatibility.
- HEVC encoding is several times slower than H.264; long 4K files take minutes.
- Browsers: Safari and Edge play HEVC; Chrome and Firefox generally do not. Keep H.264 for web embeds.
### Use cases
- Archive footage: Halve the size of a camera roll without visible loss.
- Share 4K: Make a 4K clip small enough to send.
- Apple ecosystem: Match the HEVC files iPhones already record.
- Free up a drive: Convert old H.264 recordings to HEVC.
### FAQ
Q: Will HEVC play everywhere?
A: iPhone, Mac, Windows 10+, Android 5+, modern TVs and Safari/Edge play it. Chrome and Firefox and old devices usually do not; keep H.264 for those.
Q: How much smaller will the file be?
A: Typically 40 to 50 percent smaller than H.264 at the same quality; more for simple content.
Q: Is the quality worse?
A: At the balanced preset the difference is not visible for most content. Pick high quality for footage you will edit again.
Q: Why is it slow?
A: x265 does far more work per frame than x264. It is the price of the smaller file.
